text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.38% today, continuing a sharp two-week rally that's now up 7.4%. The stock's momentum comes primarily from falling oil prices—crude dropped on September 17th after Saudi Arabia signaled it would release more supply following pipeline disruptions, easing the supply crunch that had pushed prices higher. For a refiner like Marathon, lower oil prices (the main input cost) and stable refinery utilization at 96.8% create better margins on the fuel they produce and sell.

The broader rally also reflects reduced geopolitical risk premiums. News that the U.S. may be nearing the end of its conflict with Iran, combined with Saudi Arabia's willingness to boost exports, has calmed the supply-shock concerns that had been driving oil volatility upward. Refiner stocks tend to benefit when crude prices stabilize at lower levels because they lock in better profits per barrel processed.
